evals.name: review-architecture
evals.prompt: Review the architecture shown in docs/diagrams/architecture.excalidraw. What are the biggest risks? Mark them on the diagram.
evals.expected_output: Findings checked against the code and added as red notes with a severity, each pointing at its element: shopapp-pg (and the single RabbitMQ and Redis) as single points of failure, shopapp-pg shared by keymaster-auth and ledger-orders with a cross-service foreign key, courier-worker requeueing failed messages forever with no dead-letter queue or idempotency (duplicate emails, a poison message blocks the queue), markPaid then publish as a dual write with no outbox, the synchronous gateway, keymaster-auth and Paylode chain with no timeouts, and ledger-orders trusting x-user-id. Every original element keeps its id, position, size and colours; nothing is moved or redrawn.
evals.setup: Needs a prepared project: npm run evals -- --scenario review-architecture

evals.name: review-trust-boundaries
evals.prompt: Do a security-focused review of the architecture in docs/diagrams/architecture.excalidraw: where does sensitive data or identity cross a trust boundary without enough protection? Annotate the diagram, but don't rearrange it.
evals.expected_output: Red severity notes added beside the affected elements: ledger-orders trusts the x-user-id header set by turnstile-gateway without verifying it, so anything that reaches it directly can act as any user; session tokens are checked by a call to keymaster-auth on every request; card payment details and the Paylode API key go to a third party; plain HTTP between services. The findings cite the files. Every original element keeps its id, position, size and colours.
evals.setup: Needs a prepared project: npm run evals -- --scenario review-trust-boundaries
